title: Committee of Supply – Head T (Ministry of National Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head T (Ministry of National Development)

sections.label: MND budget and CONQUAS score
sections.summary: MND's budget grows 22.2% or $4.46 billion, mainly for public housing, SERS and upgrading, while 2019 HDB CONQUAS score dropped 3.5% to 88.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Chairman, let us first look at the Budget allocation for MND.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This year, MND's budget will grow by 22.2%, or $4.46 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Increase is mainly attributed to the public housing development programme and higher spending for SERS and upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In addition, I note that the CONQUAS score for HDB flats in 2019 saw a drop of 3.5% to 88.5%, compared to 2018.

sections.label: Lease Buyback Scheme take-up
sections.summary: The member asks the Ministry to update on the take-up rate and feedback, and welcomes the Lease Buyback Scheme's extension to all flat types.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry update on the take-up rate so far and what has been the feedback received?

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am especially happy that the Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS) has been extended to all flat types.

sections.label: CBD and Strategic Development Incentives
sections.summary: The CBD Incentive and Strategic Development Incentive Schemes were launched last year to promote rejuvenation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Last year, the CBD Incentive and Strategic Development Incentive Schemes were launched to promote rejuvenation.

sections.label: Applying innovations to existing towns
sections.summary: The member asks BCA and HDB to apply such innovations rapidly to existing towns, where older infrastructure likely wastes most energy, and notes natural ventilation beats air-conditioning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Though much of this will apply to new developments, I ask that the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) and HDB look at how we can push such innovations and apply them rapidly to our existing towns, as this is where most energy wastage is likely to occur with older infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Especially amidst the lessons of this COVID-19 outbreak, natural ventilation is better than air-conditioning in reducing the chance of spread.

sections.label: ABS D review and construction support
sections.summary: The member asks the Ministry to consider temporarily revamping ABSD and to spur construction, especially SMEs, through more local rejuvenation projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I have further heard from the developers that I spoke to that they project a lean year ahead, with delays in construction as well as potential difficulties in selling their completed projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I therefore ask the Ministry to consider revamping the Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty (ABSD) temporarily, perhaps to extend the number of years subject to the state of the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I also ask the Ministry to help spur the construction industry, especially for small and medium players, by increasing the number of local rejuvenation projects such as Remaking Our Heartland (ROH), Large-Scale Town-Wide (LSTW) projects, Community Improvement Projects Committee (CIPC) projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As we rejuvenate and look towards the future, as we view with excitement the possibilities, we must never lose sight of the purpose of the Ministry of National Development (MND) – to keep to this Government's social contract with Singaporeans, so that every Singaporean will have fair access to affordable homes, accessible workplaces, liveable environments, a future-ready city and ultimately, a better Singapore for all of us and also our future generations.

sections.label: BTO waiting times and take-up
sections.summary: The member asks MND to review the three-to-four-year BTO waiting time and asks how many 2019 flats were given up and Sale of Balance take-up rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Those located at town hubs and near Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations are especially coveted by home-seekers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: However, the waiting time of three to four years for a Built-To-Order (BTO) flat is quite long, particularly so for young families with babies on the way.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would MND review this and do more to help home buyers access new flats more quickly?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In 2019, how many flats were given up by prospective buyers and what were the take-up rates of Sale Of Balance flats?

sections.label: Rejuvenating older mature estates
sections.summary: Asks what plans exist to rejuvenate older mature estates and keep them vibrant, safe, green and environmentally sustainable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: What are the plans to rejuvenate our older mature estates to keep them vibrant places to live in, and ensure that they remain safe, green and environmentally sustainable?

sections.label: Constituency-based housing safety team
sections.summary: Asks whether HDB can work with Residents' Committees, networks and advisers to set up a constituency-based housing safety team.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Second, can HDB work with the existing Residents' Committees, networks and advisers to set up a constituency-based housing safety team, or HOST, made up of residents, HDB and other partners, to gather timely feedback and statistics, and assess the potential wear-and-tear of internal structures of mature flat units before they become dangerous to occupants?

sections.label: Greenery and infrastructure trade-offs
sections.summary: Asks whether the Ministry can share plans on addressing trade-offs between greenery and infrastructure developments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The next phase of our greening journey must address this challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry share its plans on addressing the trade-offs between greenery and infrastructure developments?

sections.label: Community involvement in greening
sections.summary: Asks how the Government intends to involve the community in rejuvenating the city and greening Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share how the Government intends to involve the community in rejuvenating our city and in greening Singapore?

sections.label: Open booking of flats
sections.summary: Asks how the take-up has been for the open booking of flats launched by MND.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Related to this, how has the take-up been for the open booking of flats launched by MND?

sections.label: Review of single unwed parents' touchpoints
sections.summary: States that MND announced last year that HDB would review the touchpoints single unwed parents encounter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Two, MND announced last year that HDB would conduct a review of the touchpoints which single unwed parents would encounter.

sections.label: Proximity and CPF housing grants
sections.summary: The Proximity Housing Grant of up to $30,000 is provided to those living with or near parents or married child, and eligible first-timers can tap up to $80,000 for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: If they live with or near their parents or married child, the Proximity Housing Grant of up to $30,000 will be provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Thirdly, eligible first-timers can tap on up to $80,000 for the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG).

sections.label: 2019 COS MND rental initiatives
sections.summary: At the 2019 COS, MND announced enhancements to the $15,000 Step-Up CPF Housing Grant, rent increase waiver upon downpayment, and works to improve rental blocks and flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
sentences.text: At the 2019 COS, MND announced several initiatives, such as the enhancements to the Step-Up CPF Housing Grant of $15,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
sentences.text: This grant was extended to rental families buying a 2-room or 3-room flat in non-mature estates and the introduction of waiver of rent increases for tenants upon their downpayment for the purchase of a flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy
sentences.text: At the same 2019 COS, the Ministry announced plans to improve physical conditions of rental blocks and flats as well – works to improve the ventilation and lighting of older rental blocks to create more openings along corridors; more partitions in 1-room rental flats to enhance privacy between tenants under the Joint Singles Scheme.

sections.label: Unmarried single parents restrictions
sections.summary: Unmarried single parents remain under the Singles category, so those under 35 cannot buy apartments and those earning over $1,500 cannot apply for rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Currently, single parents who are not married are still under the "Singles" category.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: If they are under 35 years old, they cannot buy apartments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And if they earn more than $1,500, they cannot apply for rental flats.

sections.label: HDB LUP replies and alternatives
sections.summary: HDB's replies have been consistent: it will continue to study cost effective solutions to extend LUP to these blocks, and those in urgent need of direct lift access can approach HDB for alternative housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: The replies from HDB have been consistent, that is, HDB will continue to study and look for cost effective solutions to extend LUP to these blocks and Singaporeans in urgent need of direct lift access due to medical conditions or mobility issues can approach HDB for possible alternative housing arrangement.

sections.label: Cost of direct lift access
sections.summary: The Ministry informed the House that implementing direct lift access for some blocks is not marginal, with some costs as good as building a new flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
sentences.text: The Ministry had informed this House that the cost of implementing direct lift access for some blocks is not marginal, with some of the costs as good as building a new flat.

sections.label: Blocks without LUP in constituency
sections.summary: Out of 150 HDB blocks, the Member has a fair share in his constituency that were not able to get LUP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Chairman, as echoed by hon Member of the Parliament, in fact, out of these 150 HDB blocks, I have a fair share in my constituency that were not able to get this LUP.

sections.label: Home Ownership Support Team
sections.summary: The Ministry set up the Home Ownership Support Team to guide eligible HDB rental households towards home ownership, targeting 1,000 households in four or five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: Last year, the Ministry set up the Home Ownership Support Team (HST) to guide and support eligible households living in HDB rental flats to move towards home ownership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
sentences.text: HST had set the target of helping 1,000 rental households within four or five years of its launch.

sections.label: Homeless people's housing status
sections.summary: About 40% of homeless people interviewed had housing registered under their name and 15% had public rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: About 40% of the homeless people interviewed stated that they had housing registered under their name and 15% said they had public rental flats.

sections.label: Joint Singles Scheme rule
sections.summary: MND enforces the Joint Singles Scheme rule to ensure prudent use of limited land and fiscal resources.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In order to ensure prudent use of our limited land and fiscal resources, MND enforces the rule of the Joint Singles Scheme (JSS).

sections.label: Flat eligibility under scheme
sections.summary: Under this scheme only 1- or 2-bedroom flats are available, with 2-bedroom flats for families of three or more with income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under this scheme, only 1- or 2-bedroom flats are available. 2-bedroom flats are available only to families of three or more, with some income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If a family is not earning any income, they are only eligible for a 1-bedroom flat, regardless of the number of family members in that family.

sections.label: Public Rental Scheme occupancy questions
sections.summary: Questions were asked on the reason for no occupancy cap under the Public Rental Scheme and on allocating 3-room flats to families of five and over.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What is the reason for there not being an occupancy cap for homes under the Public Rental Scheme?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider allocating 3-room flats and above to families of five and over under the Public Rental Scheme?

sections.label: Special needs assisted living review
sections.summary: A question was asked whether there are plans to review areas to improve daily assisted living for people with special needs in public housing.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Further, I want to know whether there are plans to review areas that can improve people with special needs' daily assisted living in the public housing.

sections.label: Foreign contractors awarded LTA projects
sections.summary: The passage states four of seven Jurong Regional Line contracts went to foreign contractors and questions paying $6 million more for a Virgin Islands-registered one.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the LTA Jurong Regional Line Projects, for example, four out of seven contracts were awarded to foreign contractors.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Another example, LTA awarded N112 tender to a foreign contractor, even though our local contractor submitted the lowest quote.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Why pay $6 million more to a foreign contractor whose company is registered in the Virgin Islands?

sections.label: Incident casualties
sections.summary: The passage states that in that incident one person was killed and 10 others injured.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In that incident, one person was killed and 10 others injured.

sections.label: PIE viaduct collapse and BuildSG Fund
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the PIE viaduct collapse and court findings indicate a loophole, and notes the BuildSG Transformation Fund catalysed productivity innovation projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As these checks by the agencies would presumably have been done on the PIE viaduct project as well, does the collapse of the structure and the facts found by the court indicate any loophole that needs to be plugged?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the BuildSG Transformation Fund has catalysed many productivity innovation projects last year.

sections.label: Construction wages and conversion programmes
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will work with Manpower to implement the Progressive Wage Model for construction jobs and asks about PCP progress for construction PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: Will it work with the Ministry of Manpower to implement the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) for construction jobs to ensure good salaries and career outcomes?

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: How is the progress for the Professional Conversion Programmes (PCP) for PMETs in the construction industry?

sections.label: Raising Green Mark standards
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MND will consider raising Green Mark standards for new Government, commercial, and private and public residential buildings to encourage energy consumption reductions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Will MND consider raising the Green Mark standards for (a) new Government buildings; (b) all commercial buildings; and (c) all private and public residential buildings to encourage sustained reductions in overall energy consumption?

sections.label: Allowing cats in HDB flats
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Ministry will officially allow HDB flat residents to keep cats, noting the Minister earlier replied no.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: Will the Ministry consider taking the step to officially allow people staying in HDB flats to keep cats?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, Sir, earlier this year, I asked the Minister whether it is timely to consider removing the ban on keeping pet cats in HDB flats and to regulate pet cat keeping to minimise disamenities for neighbours.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Minister replied no, citing reasons of irresponsible pet ownership causing inconvenience to neighbours and unhappiness.

sections.label: CITES-based endangered species list
sections.summary: Minister Lawrence Wong replied that the list is based on CITES requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Minister Lawrence Wong replied that the list is based on the requirements of the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species of Wild Fauna and Flora (CITES).

sections.label: Malaysian bird smuggling attempt
sections.summary: A Malaysian attempted to smuggle 815 birds into Singapore, and the $10,000 maximum fine is low compared to potential profits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In August last year, a Malaysian attempted to smuggle in a record 815 birds into Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Some of these birds can trade for a few thousand dollars each so the maximum fine of $10,000 is relatively low compared to the potential profits.

sections.label: Municipal Services Office and OneService app
sections.summary: The Municipal Services Office was set up to coordinate agencies and Town Councils, and one initiative is the OneService app.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the Municipal Services Office (MSO) was set up to coordinate between agencies and Town Councils to improve the delivery of municipal services.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: One key initiative has been the set-up of OneService app.

sections.label: Tampines Town Council buying items
sections.summary: Tampines Town Council has bought some and will be trying them out.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Tampines Town Council has bought some and we will be trying them out.

sections.label: Which agency question
sections.summary: The passage asks whether it would be HDB, NEA, AVS or NParks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the Ministers for Culture, Community and Youth and Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
sentences.text: Would it be HDB, NEA or maybe AVS or maybe NParks?

sections.label: Municipal Services Productivity Fund improvements
sections.summary: Improvements through the Municipal Services Productivity Fund include Parking.sg, increasing driver convenience and reducing paper coupon litter and waste.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: Improvements through the Municipal Services Productivity Fund include Parking.sg, and this has increased convenience to drivers and reduce litter and waste generated by paper coupons.

sections.label: OneService app feedback and AI
sections.summary: The OneService app has over 200,000 users who submitted more than 460,000 feedback cases, with AI routing cases at 89% accuracy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: With the OneService app, residents can access services on-the-go.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We now have more than 200,000 app users who, collectively, submitted over 460,000 feedback cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: The use of Artificial Intelligence or AI, enables our integrated systems to route most of these cases automatically to the right agency for prompt action, with 89% accuracy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: This saves about 175 man-days a month, freeing up resources for agencies to focus on rectifying ground issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Ninety percent of cases involving multiple stakeholders found the case owner within seven days, and since 2015, the average time taken has fallen from eight-and-a-half to six days.

sections.label: OneService app post poll ratings
sections.summary: Nearly 60% of OneService app cases have post poll ratings of 4- and 5-stars.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Today, nearly 60% of our OneService app cases have post poll ratings of 4- and 5-stars.

sections.label: Yio Chu Kang littering and pigeon pilot
sections.summary: A Yio Chu Kang pilot saw an 80% reduction in related feedback, and a programme now equips community leaders and Town Councils in all towns.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: During a pilot in Yio Chu Kang to reduce high-rise littering and pigeon issues, the dedication of the Residents' Committee community leaders to educate residents personally was critical in tackling the root cause – human behaviour.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: Post-pilot, we saw an 80% reduction in related feedback.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: We have formalised a programme to equip community leaders and Town Councils in all towns with advice and resources to tackle these issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: For example, MSO is partnering MCCY in the "Love Our 'Hood" initiative that test-beds various resident participation models to co-create solutions for municipal issues in their neighbourhoods.

sections.label: City in Nature greening plans
sections.summary: The Government plans to transform Singapore into a City in Nature to provide a better quality of life amid climate change and urbanisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
sentences.text: In 2020, we will remain steadfast in our goal to deliver connected services for a connected community.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Chairman, we want to build a Singapore where the next generation can enjoy a better life than the one before.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: That is why my colleague Minister Lawrence Wong had said some time ago that "we are not done building Singapore." This spirit also motivates our push to make Singapore a City in Nature and our efforts to transform our city centre.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Today, we are a City in a Garden and, according to an MIT study, one of the world's greenest cities.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Mr Arasu Duraisamy asked about the Government's plans for the next bound of greening Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We want to transform Singapore into a City in Nature to provide Singaporeans with a better quality of life while co-existing with flora and fauna on this island.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Indeed, with climate change, more extreme weather conditions and increased urbanisation, we must do more on this front.

sections.label: 200 hectares of nature parks
sections.summary: Another 200 hectares of nature parks will be dedicated by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In all, we will dedicate another 200 hectares of nature parks by 2030.

sections.label: 40-hectare nature park at mangroves
sections.summary: NParks will establish a 40-hectare nature park at one of Singapore's few good remaining mangrove habitats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: I have kayaked there with NParks and our nature community volunteers a number of years ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It is one of the few good mangrove habitats left in Singapore and I am happy to announce that NParks will also be establishing a 40-hectare nature park there.

sections.label: More parks and gardens
sections.summary: Another 140 hectares of parks and gardens will be added over the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: You can look forward to the addition of another 140 hectares of such parks and gardens over the next five years.

sections.label: Species recovery and habitat enhancement
sections.summary: Nature groups and the community will partner on recovery plans for over 70 species and enhance 30 hectares of habitats by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, the tiger orchid is the largest orchid in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will partner nature groups and the community to carry out recovery plans for over 70 more animal and plant species and enhance 30 hectares of forest, marine and coastal habitats by 2030.

sections.label: Nature Ways and park connectors
sections.summary: Nature Ways have been planted since 2013, with aims of 300 km of Nature Ways and 500 km of park connectors by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, we have been planting Nature Ways since 2013 and, by 2030, we aim to have 300 km of Nature Ways and 500 km of park connectors.

sections.label: Doubling tree planting pace
sections.summary: Around 50,000 trees are planted a year, and the pace will double to one million trees over the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Today, we plant around the order of 50,000 trees a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We will double the pace and plant one million trees over the next 10 years.

sections.label: Stakeholders pledge tree support
sections.summary: More than 200 stakeholders have pledged support to plant more than 120,000 trees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, more than 200 stakeholders have already pledged their support to plant more than 120,000 trees.

sections.label: Singaporeans join park management
sections.summary: Over the next five years, Singaporeans can join in designing, building and managing 50 new and redeveloped parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Over the next five years, Singaporeans can join in the designing, building and management of 50 new and redeveloped parks, as my colleague Minister Lawrence Wong had announced recently.

sections.label: NParks volunteer growth target
sections.summary: There are 48,000 NParks volunteers today, with a hope to grow this to about 70,000 over the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To have 48,000 NParks volunteers working closely and passionately with us today is something we are very proud of, and we hope to grow this number to some 70,000 over the next 10 years.

sections.label: Conserving built heritage buildings
sections.summary: After a 30-year journey, close to 7,200 buildings have been conserved, with recent additions and engagement of partners and stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: As a city-state, we have to meet the national physical needs while retaining links to our past, retaining links to our national collective memory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And to-date, after a 30-year journey, we have conserved close to 7,200 buildings across our island, with some in the heartlands.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Recent additions include the former Bukit Timah Fire Station, former Railway Station Staff Quarters and SCGS campus at Emerald Hill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: And in the case of SCGS, a group of alumnae worked with stakeholders and the public to garner support for conservation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We also engage industry partners and the stakeholders in determining which building to conserve, and how we can sustain the built heritage of places.

sections.label: DfMA adoption targets
sections.summary: Teambuild saved significant time, and Singapore is on track for 40% DfMA adoption this year and 70% by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: This enabled Teambuild significant time savings, and we hope to drive greater adoption in the near future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We are on track to meet our DfMA adoption target of 40% this year, and we aim to achieve an even higher rate of 70% by 2025.

sections.label: Public Sector Construction Productivity Fund
sections.summary: $120 million will be set aside under the Public Sector Construction Productivity Fund for public sector projects adopting DfMA launched by 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To this end, we will set aside $120 million under the Public Sector Construction Productivity Fund for more public sector projects to adopt DfMA, for projects launched by 2021.

sections.label: SME digitalisation funding plan
sections.summary: BCA, IMDA and SkillsFuture Singapore developed the Construction and Facilities Management Industry Digital Plan, with $19 million to fund SMEs adopting digital solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To help our local SMEs with IDD, BCA, IMDA and SkillsFuture Singapore have developed the Construction and Facilities Management Industry Digital Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will set aside $19 million to fund SMEs to adopt digital solutions that complement basic BIM software.

sections.label: BCA Green Mark greening progress
sections.summary: Since BCA's Green Mark scheme launched in 2005, more than 40% of buildings by GFA have been greened.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since the launch of BCA’s Green Mark scheme in 2005, we have greened more than 40% of our buildings by GFA.

sections.label: Keppel Bay Tower renewable energy
sections.summary: Keppel Bay Tower will be the first commercial building fully powered by renewable energy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Keppel Bay Tower will be the first commercial building fully powered by renewable energy.

sections.label: Commercial building energy data disclosure
sections.summary: Close to 80% of commercial building owners voluntarily disclose names, addresses and energy performance data, and BCA intends to identify all buildings when publishing data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Today, close to 80% of commercial building owners voluntarily opt to disclose their buildings' names and addresses along with their energy performance data, which is published by BCA annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We intend to identify all buildings when publishing the data henceforth, so that the best performing buildings will serve as role models to encourage others to improve their own energy efficiency.

sections.label: Construction S Pass sub-DRC reduction
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister announced reducing the construction S Pass sub-DRC from 20% to 18% in January 2021 and 15% in January 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: To rebalance the share of local PMETs in construction, Deputy Prime Minister has announced a reduction in the construction S Pass sub-DRC from 20% currently to 18% in January 2021, and subsequently to 15% in January 2023.

sections.label: Participant training allowance
sections.summary: Participants will receive an allowance of up to 80% of their drawn salary during their full-time training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For the participants, they will receive an allowance of up to 80% of their drawn salary is, during their full-time training.

sections.label: Kimly BCA undergraduate sponsorship
sections.summary: Since 2015, Kimly has sponsored 15 undergraduates with BCA and introduced them to careers in the Built Environment sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Since 2015, Kimly has sponsored 15 undergraduates with BCA, and introduced them to fulfilling careers in the Built Environment sector.

sections.label: BCA building safety requirements
sections.summary: Since 2017, after the Tampines viaduct incident, BCA requires QPs and builders of higher risk projects to provide additional detailed assessments on structural stability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: BCA has introduced additional requirements since 2017, after the Tampines viaduct incident that Ms Lim mentioned, to raise our standards of building safety.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: BCA now requires the QPs and builders of higher risk projects to provide additional detailed assessments on the stability of the structure.

sections.label: Local builders winning contracts
sections.summary: Woh Hup won a $1 billion Punggol Digital District contract, and Straits Construction was in a joint venture winning a $537 million SIT contract.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For example, Woh Hup won a $1 billion contract to develop an Integrated Business Park at Punggol Digital District.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Straits Construction, another local builder, was part of a joint venture that won the $537 million contract for the Singapore Institute of Technology.

sections.label: PPVC projects delayed materials approach
sections.summary: BCA allowed 13 PPVC projects to install partially completed modules first, with finishing works done when delayed China materials arrive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: For on-going PPVC projects affected by delays to the supply of construction materials from China, BCA has adopted a facilitative approach so far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We have allowed 13 projects to install partially completed PPVC modules on-site first, and install the finishing works subsequently when the delayed materials arrive.

sections.label: Extensions, BuildSG fund, transformation agenda
sections.summary: Extensions of completion periods are considered case-by-case, appeals are few, and firms are encouraged to tap the $780 million BuildSG Transformation Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We have selectively allowed extensions of the completion period for individual projects because of extenuating circumstances, and would be prepared to consider doing so on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: But to assure the industry, we have seen just a few appeals, so it is not a big impact thus far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Even as we deal with the immediate challenges posed by COVID-19, we should not lose sight of our longer term transformation agenda.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: I strongly encourage firms to tap on the schemes available under our $780 million BuildSG Transformation Fund, so that we can all emerge stronger and better prepared for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In closing, we have made good progress, but there is certainly much more that we can do.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: We will accelerate our efforts to build more productively, create more opportunities for our firms and good jobs for our people.

sections.label: TNRM dog trapping and rehoming
sections.summary: NParks and AWGs trapped about 1,000 dogs under TNRM, rehoming or fostering over half, with hopes to rehome more Singapore Specials.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since the programme was launched, NParks and the AWGs have worked closely with the community as well as land owners on the ground to trap about 1,000 dogs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Thus far, we have managed to rehome or foster over half of the dogs trapped under TNRM, and we hope to rehome even more Singapore Specials in the coming years.

sections.label: Stray dog feedback decreased
sections.summary: Public feedback on stray dogs has decreased by more than 50% since the launch of TNRM.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In addition, I would like to share that public feedback on stray dogs has decreased by more than 50% since the launch of TNRM.

sections.label: Penalties for illegal bird smuggling
sections.summary: Under the Animals and Birds Act, penalties apply per animal or bird, with fines up to $10,000 or 12 months' jail or both per smuggled bird.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Furthermore, the penalties for illegal smuggling under the Animals and Birds Act apply per animal or bird, and not per shipment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This means that a smuggler may be liable on conviction to a fine of up to $10,000 or 12 months’ jail or both for each smuggled bird, which should be a sufficient deterrent.

sections.label: One-time dog licensing
sections.summary: NParks will introduce one-time licensing for sterilised dogs by year-end, with a $35 fee valid for the dog's life.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: To make it more convenient for pet owners, NParks will introduce a one-time licensing for sterilised dogs by the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: With one-time licensing, owners of sterilised dogs only need to apply to NParks for a licence once, instead of having to repeatedly renew their licence upon expiry.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The licence, with a one-time fee of $35, will be valid throughout the life of the dog.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: This means that if you sterilise your dog and opt for a one-time licence instead of an annual licence, you could save over $800 in licence fees over 10 years.

sections.label: Rental household waiver beneficiaries
sections.summary: Since the waiver began on 1 June 2019, close to 200 rental households have benefited.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Since the implementation of this waiver on 1 June 2019, close to 200 rental households have benefited.

sections.label: Household waivers over three years
sections.summary: In the last three years, about 5,500 households benefited from waivers intended to encourage increasing income.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In the last three years, about 5,500 households have benefited from these waivers, which are intended to encourage households to continue increasing their income.

sections.label: Steady progress supporting tenants
sections.summary: Progress has been steady, and HDB will continue to support tenants towards home ownership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: While these numbers may not seem large, the progress has been steady over the last few years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: Every family is important to us and we will continue to support our tenants towards home ownership.

sections.label: HDB flats and home ownership
sections.summary: There are more than one million HDB flats, home to about 80% of resident households, with nine in 10 owning their homes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Today, HDB flats are an integral part of our Singaporean way of life.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: There are now more than one million HDB flats, home to about 80% of our resident households.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And of these, nine in 10 own their homes.

sections.label: Enhanced CPF Housing Grant
sections.summary: First-timer families can get up to $80,000 for a new flat, or up to $160,000 for a resale flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In particular, with the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant (EHG) introduced last year, first-timer families can enjoy a grant of up to $80,000 for a new flat.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: If they buy a resale flat, they can get up to double the amount, or $160,000, in grants.

sections.label: New model for prime BTO flats
sections.summary: MND is studying a new model to sell BTO flats in prime locations at more affordable prices with tighter conditions, affecting the resale market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We cannot resolve this issue through our existing model of HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: And that is why I have shared earlier that MND is working on a new model for BTO flats in prime locations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The basic idea is to sell these flats at more affordable prices, but the flats will come with tighter conditions imposed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is a major change which we are studying and thinking through very carefully, as it will also have an impact on the resale market.

sections.label: First-timer BTO success and shorter waits
sections.summary: Almost all first-timer families succeeded within three tries for a non-mature estate BTO flat, and BTO flats with two to three year waits were introduced.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why virtually all first-timer families have been successful within their first three tries for a BTO flat in a non-mature estate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have also introduced BTO flats with shorter waiting times of two to three years, because we bring forward the construction.

sections.label: Extending open booking, ending ROF
sections.summary: Standalone ROF exercises will end, unselected SBF flats will be pooled for open booking without balloting, giving three main ways to apply.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Now that we have some experience with this open booking system, we are ready to extend it further.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, we will do away with the standalone ROF exercises and, instead, the unselected SBF flats, after the SBF exercise, will be pooled and offered directly for open booking right away, without going through another round of balloting.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This will enable home-seekers with urgent needs to access flats more quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Effectively, with this change, there will be three main ways of applying for an HDB flat.

sections.label: Waiting time under two months
sections.summary: The waiting time is now less than two months for applicants who are not particular about location.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The waiting time is now less than two months for applicants who are not particular about location.

sections.label: Divorcees can apply earlier
sections.summary: Divorcees may now apply for flats earlier, once their Interim Judgment has settled matters concerning the children and matrimonial flat.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: To ease this process, we now allow divorcees to apply for flats earlier, once their Interim Judgment has settled matters concerning the children and matrimonial flat.

sections.label: Waiving mutual agreement requirement
sections.summary: HDB will consider waiving the mutual agreement requirement if there is clear evidence that one party has already moved on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: When this happens, HDB will be prepared to consider waiving the mutual agreement requirement, if there is clear evidence that one party has already moved on.

sections.label: HDB flat buying for employed
sections.summary: HDB will let those in stable employment who can afford a flat buy a new 2-room or larger 3-room flat in a non-mature estate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, for those who are in stable employment and who can afford to buy a flat, then HDB will allow them to buy a flat – not just a new 2-room flat but also a larger 3-room flat in a non-mature estate.

sections.label: LBS public engagement and take-up
sections.summary: More is needed to help Singaporeans understand options like LBS, so public dialogues are stepped up and LBS take-up doubled from 800 households in 2018 to 1,600 last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We recognise that more needs to be done to help Singaporeans understand these different options, especially LBS, because it is relatively new and also because we have just recently extended the scheme to 5-room and larger flats, something that Mr Alex Yam, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Arasu Duraisamy highlighted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why we have been stepping up our public dialogues and engagements and I am glad to note that LBS take-up has doubled from 800 households in 2018 to 1,600 last year.

sections.label: Simplifying Silver Housing Bonus
sections.summary: The Silver Housing Bonus has several conditions, so it will be simplified and enhanced in three ways, first by removing the requirement to sell a larger flat and buy a smaller one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This is particularly the case for the Silver Housing Bonus (SHB), which comes with several conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, having studied the matter, we have decided to simplify and enhance the SHB in three ways.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: First, we will remove the requirement that seniors must sell a larger flat and buy a smaller flat.

sections.label: SHB top-up and cash bonus
sections.summary: Seniors will only need to top up the first $60,000 of their proceeds, and the maximum cash bonus will rise by 50% from $20,000 to $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The top-up required today depends on their net sales proceeds and we will simplify this such that seniors only need to top up the first $60,000 of their proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Thirdly, we will increase the maximum cash bonus by 50%, from $20,000 to $30,000.

sections.label: Lift access Housing Grant
sections.summary: Rather than SERS the entire block, a new Lift access Housing Grant of up to $30,000 will help those with medical or mobility issues buy a flat with direct lift access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: I do not think we need to SERS the entire block.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But what we will do is to offer a new Lift access Housing Grant of up to $30,000 to help those with medical or mobility issues buy a new or resale HDB flat with direct lift access.

sections.label: HDB façade repair cost sharing
sections.summary: HDB will bear half of façade repair costs, but will cover 100% if damages are clearly due to design or construction issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: On the issue of façade repairs, which Mr Pritam Singh asked about, HDB will bear half of the costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But if the damages are clearly due to design or construction issues, HDB will cover 100% of the costs.

sections.label: Flats built 1987 to 1997
sections.summary: This year, work starts on 55,000 flats, almost one quarter of flats built between 1987 and 1997.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are now ready to move on to the flats built between 1987 and 1997.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This year, we will start with almost one quarter of that or 55,000 flats.

sections.label: Age-based selection for upgrading
sections.summary: Selection is prioritised by age so older flats go first, and the HIP for 1987-1997 blocks takes around 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We are prioritising the selection by age, so that the older flats go first, and most flats should be able to get the upgrading when they are about 30 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It will take around 10 years to finish the HIP for this series of blocks built between 1987 and 1997.

sections.label: Four towns for ROH
sections.summary: This year, four more towns are selected for ROH: Bukit Merah, Queenstown, Choa Chu Kang and Ang Mo Kio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: This year, we will select another four towns for ROH.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: They are Bukit Merah, Queenstown, Choa Chu Kang and Ang Mo Kio.

sections.label: Solar capacity on HDB rooftops
sections.summary: The target rises to 70% by 2030, with solar capacity on HDB rooftops growing from 220 MWp to 540 MWp by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will increase this to 70% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: We will also deploy more efficient solar panels and aim to more than double the total solar power capacity on HDB rooftops, from 220 megawatt-peak (MWp) today to 540 MWp by 2030.

sections.label: Cool paint for HDB estates
sections.summary: A new type of paint called cool paint will be deployed to reduce heat absorbed by buildings in HDB estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Third, to help cool our HDB estates, we will deploy a new type of paint, called "cool paint", that can reduce the heat absorbed by buildings.

sections.label: Green Towns energy reduction
sections.summary: Under the Green Towns programme, the aim is to cut energy consumption in HDB towns by 15% from today's levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: With the Green Towns programme, we aim to reduce energy consumption in HDB towns by 15% from today’s levels.

sections.label: Urban Solutions and Sustainability research
sections.summary: Close to $1 billion is committed to Urban Solutions and Sustainability research, with new growth centres developed over 10 to 15 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: There are many other exciting areas where technology can make a difference in our urban transformation and improve our quality of life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why we are committing close to $1 billion in Urban Solutions and Sustainability research to build a more liveable, sustainable and resilient city.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Over the next 10 to 15 years, we will continue developing new growth centres outside the city centre to enhance Singapore’s economic infrastructure.

sections.label: Local contractors discrimination claim
sections.summary: A member says local contractors felt discriminated against, as the lowest tenderer did not get the job despite doing LTA projects.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: But I think the Minister of State has missed my point.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: I said local contractors felt that they were being discriminated against, not the foreign contractor.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: Because they submitted the lowest tender, they did not get the job, they had been doing LTA projects.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, I think you should make your clarification rather than repeat your speech.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: So, the first question is, can the Minister of State look into the discrimination of the local contractor.

sections.label: BCA review and ABSD pro-rating
sections.summary: The member asks whether BCA can review cases for this period and whether ABSD can be pro-rated when a unit is unsold.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: Instead of just case-by-case basis that BCA will consider, is it possible to review these for this period so that they do not feel so much stress during this period.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: And the fourth question, ABSD, can it be pro-rated?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: Currently, even if one unit is not sold, you have to pay up to 25% of the land cost.

sections.label: Price-Quality Method tender assurance
sections.summary: The Minister of State assures that tenders follow the Price-Quality Method, so the lowest price does not always win.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: First, I just want to assure Er Dr Lee Bee Wah that the tender methods we use today follow the Price-Quality Method or PQM, so, it is not always guaranteed that the lowest price wins.

sections.label: Local firms awarded smaller contracts
sections.summary: Between 2017 and 2019, about 90% of smaller contracts between $3 million and $85 million went to local firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If I could just share that between 2017 and 2019, local firms have been awarded a higher proportion of contracts, in terms of the smaller contracts between $3 million and $85 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: You can see about 90% of such contracted awarded to local firms.

sections.label: Proportion a decade ago
sections.summary: A decade ago, the proportion was only 40%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: A decade ago, we used to have only a 40% proportion.

sections.label: ABSD obligations case-by-case
sections.summary: Developers who have difficulty meeting their ABSD obligations will be handled on a case-by-case basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: If developers have difficulty meeting their ABSD obligations, we will take it on a case-by-case basis.

sections.label: MSO monitors case closure time
sections.summary: MSO monitors the time taken to close cases to deliver good public services effectively and in a timely way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: MSO does monitor the time taken to close the case because it is our objective to ensure that we deliver good Public Service, good public municipal services in an effective and timely way.

sections.label: Post-case poll stipulated
sections.summary: A post-case poll has been stipulated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
sentences.text: With that in mind, we have stipulated, what we call a post-case poll.

sections.label: Pet bird trade enforcement request
sections.summary: NParks was asked not to forget the pet bird trade when stepping up enforcement, and ICA with NParks seized 815 birds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: It is actually a request that NParks do not forget about the pet bird trade when stepping up the enforcement on the regulations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: That is why, with the efforts of ICA together with NParks, they had seized the shipment of 815 birds that the Member mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: In 2016, it was eight cases; in 2019, it was two cases, one of which was cited by Mr Yee.

sections.label: Divorced parents subsidised housing rule
sections.summary: The rule does not allow a child's name to be with both divorced parents for subsidised housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the short answer is yes, we are very reasonable people and we want the best for the child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, in a case where indeed, both have divorced, they have one child, it is shared care and control and each individual wants subsidised housing, today, the rule does not allow the child's name to be together with both parents.

sections.label: Lift access grant for HDB owners
sections.summary: The grant is available to all HDB owners with mobility issues whose flats lack lift access, to help them get a flat with lift access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the grant will be made available to all HDB owners with immediate effect, once this has been announced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, anyone who owns a HDB flat, regardless of whether you are first-timer, second-timer, nth-timer, but you are the owner of a flat and your flat does not lift access, and you have mobility issues, that is the condition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Then, we will help you get a new flat or a resale flat where there is lift access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: And the grant will be extended to that owner to facilitate that transaction.

sections.label: JSS partitions and privacy
sections.summary: JSS now has partitions, more privacy and flexibility, and those with medical conditions may be considered to stay alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: JSS today is different from what it used to be, because now we have partitions, we provide more privacy, we give flexibility and anyone that comes with medical conditions with a reason that they need to stay alone, we are prepared to consider, we are prepared to be flexible and allow them to stay on their own.

sections.label: Studying the matter
sections.summary: The speaker says they did state that they will study this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Just to make it clear to the Member as well, I did say we will study this.

sections.label: S Pass reduction programmes
sections.summary: On the S Pass reduction, various programmes have been put in place.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: The second one on the S Pass reduction, certainly we have put in place various programmes, as I shared earlier.

sections.label: PWM, DRC and amendment withdrawal
sections.summary: PWM gives ITE workers better-paying jobs, the sub-DRC is cut, and the amendment is withdrawn.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Even for the lift too, we have put in the PWM to ensure that our steady stream of workers coming through from ITE also get better-paying jobs, so that they do not either get substituted by cheaper foreign labour or have to go elsewhere for better-paying jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: At the same time, we recognise that there are some jobs at the work permit level that we need to continually depend on our foreign workforce for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: Therefore, you do not see us cutting the whole Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC), it is just the sub-DRC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: Chairman, I thank the 22 fellow Members who filed a diverse range of cuts, and Minister Lawrence, Second Minister Desmond Lee and Minister Grace, Minister of State Zaqy and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling for their comprehensive replies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: We are reasonable people, so I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
